title: Chemical equilibrium 1: reversible, Q and K - 123 school
heading: Chemical equilibrium 1: reversible, Q and K
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.

questions.q: What is a reaction that goes to completion?
questions.a: A reaction in which the starting substances (almost) completely disappear and only reaction products remain

questions.q: What is a reversible reaction?
questions.a: A reaction that can proceed in both directions. You write it with the sign ⇌

questions.q: What is a chemical equilibrium?
questions.a: A state in which the forward and the reverse reaction go equally fast, so the concentrations no longer change

questions.q: Why is a chemical equilibrium called dynamic?
questions.a: Because the forward and reverse reactions keep going; they just go equally fast

questions.q: Are the concentrations of all substances in an equilibrium equal?
questions.a: No. They are constant, but not necessarily equal to each other

questions.q: What must you do with a system to let it reach an equilibrium?
questions.a: Close it (closed system) so that no substances can escape

questions.q: Give the equilibrium condition of N<sub>2</sub> (g) + 3 H<sub>2</sub> (g) ⇌ 2 NH<sub>3</sub> (g)
questions.a: K = [NH<sub>3</sub>]<sup>2</sup> / ([N<sub>2</sub>] · [H<sub>2</sub>]<sup>3</sup>)

questions.q: Give the equilibrium condition of H<sub>2</sub> (g) + I<sub>2</sub> (g) ⇌ 2 HI (g)
questions.a: K = [HI]<sup>2</sup> / ([H<sub>2</sub>] · [I<sub>2</sub>])

questions.q: Give the equilibrium condition of 2 NO<sub>2</sub> (g) ⇌ N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> (g)
questions.a: K = [N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub>] / [NO<sub>2</sub>]<sup>2</sup>

questions.q: Give the equilibrium condition of 2 SO<sub>2</sub> (g) + O<sub>2</sub> (g) ⇌ 2 SO<sub>3</sub> (g)
questions.a: K = [SO<sub>3</sub>]<sup>2</sup> / ([SO<sub>2</sub>]<sup>2</sup> · [O<sub>2</sub>])

questions.q: Which substances do you leave out of the equilibrium condition?
questions.a: Solids and pure liquids (and the solvent water)

questions.q: Give the equilibrium condition of CaCO<sub>3</sub> (s) ⇌ CaO (s) + CO<sub>2</sub> (g)
questions.a: K = [CO<sub>2</sub>]

questions.q: Give the equilibrium condition of C (s) + CO<sub>2</sub> (g) ⇌ 2 CO (g)
questions.a: K = [CO]<sup>2</sup> / [CO<sub>2</sub>]

questions.q: What is the concentration quotient Q?
questions.a: The same fraction as K, but with the concentrations at any moment (not necessarily at equilibrium)

questions.q: What holds for Q and K in an equilibrium?
questions.a: Q = K

questions.q: Q is smaller than K. In which direction does the reaction go overall?
questions.a: To the right (more products are formed) until Q = K

questions.q: Q is greater than K. In which direction does the reaction go overall?
questions.a: To the left (more starting substances are formed) until Q = K

questions.q: What does the value of K depend on?
questions.a: Only on the reaction and the temperature

questions.q: Does a catalyst change the value of K?
questions.a: No. A catalyst only makes the equilibrium be reached faster

questions.q: What does a very large K (much greater than 1) mean?
questions.a: At equilibrium there are mainly reaction products

questions.q: What does a very small K (much smaller than 1) mean?
questions.a: At equilibrium there are mainly starting substances

questions.q: For H<sub>2</sub> + I<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2 HI at equilibrium [H<sub>2</sub>] = 0.10 mol/L, [I<sub>2</sub>] = 0.10 mol/L and [HI] = 0.40 mol/L. Calculate K
For 2 SO<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2 SO<sub>3</sub> at equilibrium [SO<sub>2</sub>] = 0.20 mol/L, [O<sub>2</sub>] = 0.10 mol/L and [SO<sub>3</sub>] = 0.40 mol/L. Calculate K

Assume that for N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> ⇌ 2 NO<sub>2</sub> K = 0.20. At a certain moment [N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub>] = 0.50 mol/L and [NO<sub>2</sub>] = 0.10 mol/L. In which direction does the reaction go?
questions.a: Q = 0.10<sup>2</sup> / 0.50 = 0.020. Q is smaller than K, so to the right

questions.q: For A + B ⇌ C, K = 4.0. At equilibrium [A] = 0.20 mol/L and [B] = 0.50 mol/L. Calculate [C]
In a vessel of 1.0 L you start with 1.00 mol H<sub>2</sub> and 1.00 mol I<sub>2</sub>. At equilibrium [HI] = 1.60 mol/L. Calculate K for H<sub>2</sub> + I<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2 HI
questions.a: 0.80 mol H<sub>2</sub> and 0.80 mol I<sub>2</sub> react, so [H<sub>2</sub>] = [I<sub>2</sub>] = 0.20 mol/L. K = 1.60<sup>2</sup> / 0.20<sup>2</sup> = 64
